description: ``tar -xf ARCHIVE -C DIR`` extracts arbitrary file trees into ``DIR``. An attacker who stages an archive at ``/tmp/x.tar`` and then runs ``tar -xf /tmp/x.tar -C tools/cc/hooks/`` can land an entire replacement hook tree without triggering the hook (which had no tar extractor). Same applies to ``-C DIR`` placed before ``-xf`` and to the long form ``--directory=DIR``. Combined with BC-019/BC-017, this completes the ``stage-then-extract`` class. Note: zip-slip (BC-010) is a related but distinct class — that one is about archive members escaping the extraction dir via ``..``; this one is about the extraction dir itself being protected.
